clue.text: Grovelled after a second and dashed off

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
to crawl is to grovel servilely

explanation.surface: Someone grovelled briefly, then hurried off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the grovelling word behind the abbreviation for a second.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing scrawled is hastily and untidily written, just as a note dashed off is.

clue.text: This herb makes many sick

blocks.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A warning that a certain herb makes lots of people unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords often use 'many' for a large Roman numeral such as D (500) or M (1000).
explanation.definitionFit: Dill is a feathery aromatic plant used in cooking, a common culinary herb.

clue.text: Irritable et cetera in you past?

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: thy is the old-fashioned form of 'your', the second person in past English
ETC is the usual abbreviation for et cetera

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether some irritability lies in someone's history.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation sits inside the archaic possessive: T(ETC)HY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy is a synonym for irritable: easily annoyed and short-tempered.

clue.text: Caressed in street, blushing, round the green light

indicators.note: one word going round another wraps it, enclosing it inside

blocks.note: ST is the standard abbreviation for street
someone blushing goes red
giving the green light means saying OK, granting approval

explanation.surface: A blushing couple caressing in the street at a traffic light.
explanation.walkthrough: The colour of blushing wraps the approval: R(OK)ED, after the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroke someone is to caress them with gentle movements of the hand, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Dreamily blest any eccentric

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so these letters are set out in an unusual order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of a dreamy, blessed eccentric person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' looks like a noun for the dreamer, but it signals the rearrangement of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting absently means with the mind elsewhere, as if in a daydream.

clue.text: Large drink being had by a spy

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: the thing a spy has

blocks.note: a double is a large measure of spirits
being, in the sense of existence, is life

explanation.surface: A spy downing a big drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' looks like a verb joining the parts, but it supplies the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: A spy leads a secret existence alongside an apparently ordinary one, which is a double life.

clue.text: It's clever, but you can make a doctor love it

blocks.note: taken as written
DR is the abbreviation for doctor
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A playful boast about turning a doctor's love into something clever.
explanation.walkthrough: Love meaning O comes from the nil score in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and quick-witted, a close synonym of clever.

clue.text: A mishap, so I'd better share the stress

indicators.note: to share something is to get inside it alongside its owner, so these words go into that

blocks.note: an accent is the stress placed on a syllable
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: After a mishap, someone resolves to share the stress of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The I'D goes into the stress word: ACC(ID)ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unplanned unfortunate event, which is what a mishap is.

clue.text: Being thoughtful by holding the door back

indicators.note: going back means reading the door word from right to left
holding something means having it inside, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: Someone lost in thought while holding a door open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link but supplies the outer letters: B(ROOD)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Broody can mean moody and pensive, brooding over things, so deep in thought.

clue.text: Lose power and surrender

blocks.note: first meaning: a government or ruler ... from office
second meaning

explanation.surface: A regime losing its grip and capitulating.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are uses of the verb: a regime is toppled, and a besieged city is captured or yields.

clue.text: Incomprehensible subject? Return it to the library!

blocks.note: first meaning: an idiom for a topic one cannot understand
second meaning, playful: a book shut and done with, ready to go back

explanation.surface: A frustrated reader gives up on a baffling subject and sends the volume back.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: a volume you have finished with and shut is literally a shut book.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something or someone you cannot understand at all, like an unopened volume.

clue.text: Calm surrounds a little daughter from dawn to dusk

indicators.note: one word surrounding another encloses it within its letters

blocks.note: to allay is to calm fears or worries
D is the short form of daughter

explanation.surface: A tranquil scene of a small daughter from morning till night.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation goes into the verb: ALL(D)AY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting the whole day means from sunrise to sunset, the whole span of daylight.

clue.text: Stupid server may lift food

blocks.note: dumb means stupid in informal use
a waiter serves at table

explanation.surface: A slow-witted waiter who may be carrying dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a dim member of staff; the answer is a mechanical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbwaiter is a small lift used to carry dishes between floors of a restaurant or house.

clue.text: A passionate appeal to scoff in the doorway

indicators.note: something put in a place is set inside it

blocks.note: an entry is a doorway or entrance
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: Someone at the door pleading to be allowed to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoff' here is the British informal verb for gobbling food, not mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request or plea, exactly a heartfelt appeal.

clue.text: Strange fellows starting to talk a bit

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: odd means strange
fellows are men
the opening letter of talk

explanation.surface: Peculiar men beginning to chat a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' looks like an adverb about talking, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover scrap or small piece, so a bit of something.

clue.text: Fertilisers maybe getting money raised with fees

indicators.note: in a down clue something raised is lifted upward, so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: tin is old British slang for money
rates are charges or fees

explanation.surface: Farmers paying more for fertiliser as charges rise.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin for money is dated British slang; 'maybe' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrates are compounds widely spread on fields as fertiliser, so they are one kind.

clue.text: Properly close to justice

blocks.note: by means near or beside
right is what is just

explanation.surface: Behaving correctly, almost with justice.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by right means doing it rightfully or as one is entitled, so in a proper way.

clue.text: A tirade, one telephoned, interrupting the tone

indicators.note: what interrupts something breaks into its middle, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a hue is a tone or shade of colour
a means one
rang is the past tense of ring, to telephone

explanation.surface: Someone phones and launches into a rant, cutting through the dialling tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tone' sounds like the phone line, but here it means a shade of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A harangue is a long, aggressive lecture or speech, which is what a tirade is.

clue.text: Taught little boy to hold water

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one word is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: Ted is a short form of the boy's name Edward
rain is water from the sky

explanation.surface: Teaching a small boy to carry water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little boy' is a common signal for a short boy's name such as Ted.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to teach them a skill, so trained and taught are synonyms in the past tense.

clue.text: Overnight guests may be in such trouble in the bathroom

blocks.clueFragment: Overnight guests may be in such trouble in the bathroom
blocks.note: surface reading: visitors who stay over may find themselves in difficulty
setter's reading: what guests use up in the bathroom is the heated supply, and the same phrase is an idiom for trouble

explanation.surface: A host's worry about guests running out of something in the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is both the idiom for being in trouble and the literal heated supply that guests use up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in this idiomatically means being in serious difficulty or disgrace.

clue.text: Yes, rot destroyed shellfish

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Confirmation that decay has ruined a batch of seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster is a bivalve mollusc, one kind of edible shellfish.

clue.text: Cry? About her fruit?

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is placed round the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Puzzled questions: is she weeping, and over some fruit?
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry is a small round stone fruit.

clue.text: Abandon container with celery half gone

indicators.note: with half gone, only half of the word remains and the rest is dropped

blocks.note: a can is a container
taken as written before cutting

explanation.surface: Throwing out a tub of celery that is half eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Celery has six letters, so half of it is its first three.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel a plan is to abandon or call it off.

clue.text: Like good food? Hope it is then

blocks.note: as means like
pi is short for pious, so good
a ration is an allowance of food

explanation.surface: A diner asking whether they will like the meal and hoping so.
explanation.walkthrough: PI for good comes from pious; the clue reads like one question about a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiration is an ambition or hope for the future.

clue.text: The Karenina woman had to decide which way to go!

indicators.text: had to decide which way to go
indicators.note: someone unsure which way to go could equally head either way, so the name reads the same in both directions

blocks.note: the heroine of Tolstoy's novel, whose first name reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: Tolstoy's heroine facing a fateful choice of direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Tolstoy's heroine famously agonised over her choices; her first name reads identically forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Karenina is the title character of Tolstoy's novel, so her given name is the woman meant.

clue.text: These are sometimes ruined by the cast

definitions.text: These are sometimes ruined by the cast

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged; the definite article is surface only

explanation.surface: A sigh about poor actors spoiling parts of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and the same words also rearrange the final word's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plays are divided into sections performed by actors, which a weak company can spoil.

clue.text: It's hard always in the southeast

indicators.note: a word in something sits within it

blocks.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast
ever means always

explanation.surface: A grumble that life is always tough in the south-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means harsh or difficult, as in a hard winter or severe weather.

clue.text: Prevent fulmination, keeping busy

indicators.note: the words keep the answer inside them, holding it within their letters

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Advice to stop an angry outburst by staying occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventful day is one full of happenings, a busy one.
